Tutorial 6: Linking Socioeconomic Data

climasus4r Team

13/09/2026

Source: vignettes/06-socioeconomico.Rmd
06-socioeconomico.Rmd

Objective

By the end of this tutorial you will be able to link Brazilian Demographic Census variables to health data that has already been spatialized and compute standardized socioeconomic and epidemiological indicators. You will learn to:

  • discover which census variables are available with sus_census_select();
  • download and aggregate census microdata (or census tracts) to the municipal level and join them to the health data with sus_census_join() (via the censobr package);
  • compute indicators such as aging, dependency, and sanitation coverage — with confidence intervals — using sus_socio_compute_indicators();
  • query the full indicator catalog with sus_socio_list_indicators().

The socioeconomic linkage is the sixth stage of the climasus4r pipeline. It requires the data to have already gone through the spatial join (Tutorial 5), since the linkage key is the municipality’s 7-digit IBGE code (code_muni_7).

Scientific context

Climate and health studies can rarely treat the population as homogeneous. Social vulnerability — poverty, low education, poor sanitation, an aging age structure — modulates the relationship between environmental exposure (temperature, pollution) and health outcomes, acting both as a confounder and as an effect modifier (Gouveia, Hajat & Armstrong, 2003; Hajat, O’Connor & Kosatsky, 2010). Elderly people living in households lacking adequate infrastructure, for example, suffer more during heat waves.

In Brazil, the official source for these variables is IBGE’s Demographic Census, accessible programmatically through the censobr package (Pereira & Barbosa, 2023). climasus4r wraps this access in sus_census_join(), downloading the chosen dataset, filtering only the municipalities present in the health data before loading into memory (Arrow/Parquet optimization), aggregating the microdata to the municipal level, and performing the join on the geographic key.

From these variables, sus_socio_compute_indicators() computes a set of standardized indicators (demographic, socioeconomic, mortality, morbidity, maternal-and-child health, and health-resource indicators), each with its formula, multiplier, and uncertainty method declared in an internal catalog.

Methodological caveat (ecological bias). Municipal indicators describe the aggregate, not the individual: associations observed between a municipality’s mean vulnerability and its health outcomes do not automatically transfer to individuals (ecological fallacy). The aggregation scale also matters — the same phenomenon can change sign depending on the unit (modifiable areal unit problem, MAUP). Use these indicators as area-level covariates, not as individual attributes.

Guiding case. We investigate temperature and health outcomes in the elderly (60+) in the São Paulo Metropolitan Region, 2014–2019. In Tutorial 5 we spatialized respiratory (J00–J99) and cardiovascular (I00–I99) deaths by municipality. Here we link 2010 Census variables and compute vulnerability indicators (aging, dependency, sewage and water coverage) that will serve as covariates/effect modifiers in the climate–health modeling of the upcoming tutorials.

Data used

Item Value Role in the case
Input dados/caso_espacial.rds (Tutorial 5) Spatialized deaths by municipality (RMSP)
Census dataset "population" (2010 Census) Population by municipality (elderly, young, working-age)
Linkage key code_muni_7 (IBGE, 7 digits) Links health × census
Indicators aging, dependency, sewage, water Municipal vulnerability
Output dados/caso_socio.rds Input for Tutorial 7 (INMET climate)

All data are public and real (IBGE/Census via censobr).

Full pipeline

The blocks below reproduce what the script scripts/tutorial_06_socioeconomico.R executes. Start by loading the package and the chained input:

library(climasus4r)

# Saída do Tutorial 5: óbitos espacializados por município (stage "spatial",
# com a coluna code_muni_7 — chave do vínculo).
caso_espacial <- readRDS("dados/caso_espacial.rds")

Step 1 — Discover census variables (sus_census_select())

Before downloading the census, it is worth discovering the codes of the variables. In interactive use, output = "browser" opens a searchable HTML interface; in scripts, prefer output = "codes", which returns a vector of codes without opening the browser:

# Códigos das variáveis de população do Censo 2010 (uso programático):
vars_pop <- sus_census_select(
  dataset = "population",  # "all", "population", "households", "families", ...
  year    = 2010,           # 2010 (padrão) ou 2000
  output  = "codes",        # "browser" (padrão), "console" ou "codes"
  lang    = "pt",
  verbose = FALSE
)
head(vars_pop)

Step 2 — Link the census (sus_census_join())

sus_census_join() downloads the chosen dataset via censobr, filters only the municipalities present in code_muni_7, aggregates the microdata to the municipal level (aggregation_fun), and performs the left_join. It requires the data to be at stage >= "spatial":

caso_enriquecido <- sus_census_join(
  df              = caso_espacial,
  dataset         = "population",     # "population"/"households"/"families"/
                                       # "mortality"/"emigration"/"tracts"
  year            = 2010,             # 2010 (padrão) ou 2000
  census_vars     = head(vars_pop, 6),# NULL = todas (não recomendado)
  aggregation_fun = "sum",            # "sum","mean","median","min","max","sd",
                                       # "q25","q75","q95","q99"
  use_cache       = TRUE,             # cache local do censobr
  cache_dir       = "~/.climasus4r_cache/census",
  lang            = "pt",
  verbose         = TRUE
)

Each aggregated numeric variable receives the suffix of the aggregation mode (e.g., V0001 aggregated by sum becomes V0001_sum). If the input is an sf object, the geometry is preserved in the output.

To use census tract data instead of microdata, switch to dataset = "tracts" and choose the table in tracts_dataset (e.g., "Basico", "DomicilioRenda", "Pessoa03"):

caso_setores <- sus_census_join(
  df             = caso_espacial,
  dataset        = "tracts",
  tracts_dataset = "Basico",   # "Basico","Domicilio01/02","DomicilioRenda",
                                # "Pessoa01"..."Pessoa13","ResponsavelRenda", ...
  year           = 2010,
  lang           = "pt"
)

Step 3 — Query the indicator catalog (sus_socio_list_indicators())

Before computing, inspect what is available. Without a network, it returns a tibble with id, name, category, required_cols, formula, multiplier, unit, uncertainty_method, and source:

catalogo <- sus_socio_list_indicators(lang = "pt")

# Filtrar por categoria, se desejar:
sus_socio_list_indicators(lang = "pt", category = "mortality")

Step 4 — Compute indicators (sus_socio_compute_indicators())

Indicators are defined in formula space (names such as pop_elderly, total_hh). Since the columns coming from the census have different names (e.g., V0001_sum), use col_mapping to connect formula names to actual columns:

caso_socio <- sus_socio_compute_indicators(
  df               = caso_enriquecido,
  indicators       = c("aging_index", "dependency_ratio",
                       "sewage_connection_rate", "water_connection_rate"),
  col_mapping = list(
    pop_elderly = "pop_65_plus_sum",  # aponte para as colunas agregadas reais
    pop_young   = "pop_0_14_sum",
    pop_working = "pop_15_64_sum",
    pop_total   = "V0001_sum",
    total_hh    = "V003_sum",
    hh_sewage   = "V0207_sum",
    hh_water    = "V0208_sum"
  ),
  confidence_level = 0.95,   # IC de Poisson (taxas) / Wilson (proporções)
  add_ci           = TRUE,   # adiciona colunas ind_<id>_low / ind_<id>_high
  lang             = "pt",
  verbose          = TRUE
)

Each computed indicator becomes a column ind_<id> (e.g., ind_aging_index), and — when the uncertainty method is not "none" and add_ci = TRUE — also ind_<id>_low and ind_<id>_high. If indicators = NULL, the function automatically detects all indicators whose required columns are present (after col_mapping); indicators lacking the necessary columns are skipped with a warning, never interrupting execution.

At the end, caso_socio is saved (with save_tbl() in the script) and feeds Tutorial 7 (Station-Based Climate — INMET).

Function characteristics

sus_census_select()

Explorer for census variables. Helps discover codes to use in sus_census_join(census_vars = ...).

Argument Essential? Description
dataset recommended "all" (default), "population", "households", "families", "mortality", "emigration", "tracts"
year optional 2010 (default) or 2000
output recommended "browser" (interactive HTML, default), "console", or "codes" (vector)
lang optional "pt" (default), "en", "es"
verbose optional Informative messages

Return: with "codes", a character vector of codes; with "browser"/"console", invisibly returns a data.frame (and opens/prints the interface).

sus_census_join()

Links census variables (microdata or tracts) to health data. Wrapper around censobr::read_population(), read_households(), read_tracts(), etc.

Argument Essential? Description
df yes climasus_df/sf at stage >= "spatial", with code_muni_7
dataset yes "population" (default), "households", "families", "mortality", "emigration", "tracts"
tracts_dataset only tracts Tract table: "Basico" (default), "DomicilioRenda", "Pessoa01..13", …
year optional 2010 (default) or 2000
census_vars recommended Vector of codes (use sus_census_select()); NULL = all
aggregation_fun optional "sum" (default), "mean", "median", "min", "max", "sd", "q25", "q75", "q95", "q99"
join_muni_col optional IBGE code column; NULL detects SUS patterns
use_cache / cache_dir recommended censobr cache (~/.climasus4r_cache/census)
translate_columns / standardize_values optional Translates names and labels (default TRUE)
lang / verbose optional Language and messages

Return: the same df (or sf) with additional census columns (suffixed by the aggregation mode, e.g., _sum); metadata advances to stage = "census".

sus_socio_compute_indicators()

Computes standardized indicators over the present columns, with optional confidence intervals.

Argument Essential? Description
df yes climasus_df at stage >= "spatial" (output of sus_census_join())
indicators optional Vector of IDs; NULL = all computable (auto-detection)
col_mapping recommended Named list: formula name → actual column (e.g., list(total_hh = "V003_sum"))
confidence_level optional Confidence level (default 0.95)
add_ci optional TRUE (default) adds ind_<id>_low/_high
lang / verbose optional Language and messages

Return: the climasus_df with columns ind_<id> (and _low/_high where applicable); sus_meta updated to type = "indicators".

sus_socio_list_indicators()

Lists the full indicator catalog. Does not depend on network access.

Argument Description
lang Language of the names: "pt" (default), "en", "es"
category Filter by category (e.g., "demographic", "mortality"); NULL = all

Return: a tibble with id, name, category, required_cols, formula, multiplier, unit, uncertainty_method, source.

Formulas

Indicators are computed as a ratio (rate/proportion) multiplied by a scaling factor. In general form:

indicador=(numeradordenominador)×m \text{indicador} = \left(\frac{\text{numerador}}{\text{denominador}}\right) \times m

where mm is the multiplier declared in the catalog. Examples used in the guiding case:

Índice de Envelhecimento=popidosapopjovem×100 \text{Índice de Envelhecimento} = \frac{\text{pop}_{\text{idosa}}}{\text{pop}_{\text{jovem}}} \times 100

Razão de Dependência=popjovem+popidosapopativa×100 \text{Razão de Dependência} = \frac{\text{pop}_{\text{jovem}} + \text{pop}_{\text{idosa}}}{\text{pop}_{\text{ativa}}} \times 100

Cobertura de Esgoto=domicílios com esgotototal de domicílios×100 \text{Cobertura de Esgoto} = \frac{\text{domicílios com esgoto}}{\text{total de domicílios}} \times 100

Confidence intervals. For rates based on event counts (mortality, incidence, hospitalizations), the exact Poisson interval (Garwood) is used, based on the Gamma distribution:

ICinf=1nχα/2;2k2/2,ICsup=1nχ1−α/2;2(k+1)2/2 \text{IC}_{\text{inf}} = \frac{1}{n}\,\chi^2_{\alpha/2;\,2k}\big/2, \qquad \text{IC}_{\text{sup}} = \frac{1}{n}\,\chi^2_{1-\alpha/2;\,2(k+1)}\big/2

For proportions (coverage rates, %), the Wilson score interval is used:

p̂±z1+z2/n[z2n+p̂(1−p̂)n+z24n2] \hat{p} \pm \frac{z}{1 + z^2/n}\left[\frac{z}{2n} + \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n} + \frac{z^2}{4n^2}}\right]

with z=z1−α/2z = z_{1-\alpha/2}, kk the number of events, and nn the denominator. Ratios with complex numerators or direct indices (e.g., Gini) do not receive a CI (uncertainty_method = "none").
